title: Juniper and the Spire
premise: August Thornbury's quiet life of selling outlawed charms shatters when a century-old prophecy book names tonight as the night the Spire falls — and the prophecy begins rewriting itself around her every choice. To stop the collapse of the covenant between the human city and the hidden realm beneath it, she must gather three estranged keepers, each holding a shard of the broken pact and each nursing a grievance against the temple that bound her. But the Spire's fall was never an accident: the temple's high canon engineered it to hoard magic for himself, and he will erase August's memories — the same way he erased her mother's — to keep his secret. In the end, August reforges the covenant not with power but by offering her own memories as its binding ink, saving both realms while choosing which pieces of herself are worth forgetting.
about_author: Y. M. Amberdale is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing damaged manuscripts in a coastal university library before turning to fiction full-time. They write fantasy about ordinary people caught in machinery far older than themselves, usually over too much tea.

chapters.title: The Date That Was Written
chapters.summary: August's POV. While copying inventory in the temple archive, August discovers her exact name and today's date in a sealed prophecy book, minutes before temple enforcers arrive to burn it — and her. She escapes into the undercity with the book and a reluctant ally, pickpocket-turned-guide Fen. The emotional beat: terror giving way to a fierce, unfamiliar sense of being chosen rather than trapped.

chapters.title: Three Shards, Three Grudges
chapters.summary: Alternating between August and Fen. The pair track the covenant's three keeper-shards: a disgraced healer in the flooded quarter, a stone-singer imprisoned by the temple, and a feral child who speaks only in the old tongue. Each keeper tests August's motives, forcing her to admit she wants freedom from her debt more than justice. The beat: found family forming through friction, and August's first taste of real power — and how good it feels.

chapters.title: What the High Canon Erased
chapters.summary: August's POV. The shards assembled, August confronts High Canon Vess and learns the truth: he orchestrated the covenant's breaking, and he erased her mother's memories when she discovered it. Vess offers August her mother's stolen memories in exchange for walking away. The climax builds as she refuses, the keepers rally, and the Spire begins to fall on schedule. The beat: grief weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: Ink Made of Memory
chapters.summary: Full ensemble POV. At the Spire's heart, August writes the new covenant using her own memories as binding ink — sacrificing her childhood with her mother, the one thing Vess could never take. The covenant holds; Vess is unmade by the pact he broke; the keepers become August's family by choice, not prophecy. The beat: bittersweet triumph — she cannot remember what she saved, but everyone she loves remembers it for her.
